learn.hook: How far is your school? A few steps, a few hundred metres or a few kilometres? Let's become distance detectives!
points: We measure short lengths in millimetres (mm) and centimetres (cm), like a pencil or an eraser.
We measure longer lengths in metres (m), like a room, a saree or a cricket pitch.
We measure long distances in kilometres (km), like the road from one town to another.
When you use a ruler, start from the 0 mark. If you start at another mark, subtract.
To find the length of a route, add the lengths of its parts.

example.q: Harpreet walks 350 m from home to the shop and then 450 m from the shop to the park. How far does she walk?

learn.reallife: Road signs show kilometres to the next town. Tailors measure cloth in metres and centimetres.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put these from shortest to longest

quiz.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so centimetres fit best.
steps: A pencil is a short length.
Short lengths are measured in cm or mm; km and m are for long ones, litres is not length.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit for long distances, or a unit that is not for length

quiz.q: Which unit is best for the distance from Delhi to Agra?
quiz.explain: Towns are far apart, so we use kilometres.
steps: Delhi and Agra are towns far apart.
Long distances between towns are measured in kilometres.
quiz.mistake: Thinks metres are enough for long distances between towns

quiz.q: An eraser lies on a ruler. It starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at the 7 cm mark. How long is it?
steps: End mark 7 cm, start mark 2 cm
quiz.mistake: Reads only the end mark and forgets the eraser did not start at 0

quiz.q: Which unit should Meena use to measure the length of her classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is a few metres long, so metres fit best.
steps: A classroom is a few metres long.
mm is too small, km is too big, grams is not a length.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a unit that is far too small or far too big

quiz.q: Kabir takes 10 steps. Each step is about 50 cm. About how far does he walk?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change centimetres into metres

quiz.q: Meena's school is 2 km from home. She walks there and back every day. How far does she walk each day?
quiz.explain: There and back is the distance two times: 2 km + 2 km = 4 km.

quiz.q: How many millimetres make 1 centimetre?
quiz.explain: Look at a ruler: each centimetre has 10 small marks. 1 cm = 10 mm.
steps: On a ruler, each centimetre has 10 small marks.

quiz.q: Which road is the longest?
quiz.explain: 1 km = 1,000 m, which is more than 900 m. 1,500 cm is only 15 m.
steps: Write all lengths in metres: 1 km = 1,000 m; 1,500 cm = 15 m.
1,000 m is the biggest, so the road of 1 km is the longest.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the biggest number and ignores the unit

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly to Grandma's village. He asks: 'How do people measure how far things are?'
teach.praise: Wow! Small things in cm, rooms in metres and far places in km. I'll fly 3 km!
teach.nudge: Which unit would you use for a short thing, and which for a far-away town?

revise.summary: Short lengths are measured in mm and cm, longer lengths in metres and long distances between places in kilometres. Measure from the 0 mark and add the parts of a route.
focus: Choose the best unit for a length
Read a ruler when the object does not start at 0
Find the length of a route by adding its parts
remember: If you start at another mark, subtract: 7 cm − 2 cm = 5 cm
traps: Don't look only at the biggest number; check the unit: 1 km is more than 900 m.
Don't count only one way for 'there and back'.

learn.hook: A saree is 550 cm long. Is that more or less than 6 metres? Converting units will tell you!
points: 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm.
1 km = 1,000 m, so half a kilometre is 500 m.
Big unit to small unit: multiply. 3 m = 3 × 100 = 300 cm.
Small unit to big unit: divide. 4,000 m = 4,000 ÷ 1,000 = 4 km.
Mixed units: 2 m 35 cm = 200 cm + 35 cm = 235 cm.
learn.reallife: Marathon runners talk about 42 km. Tailors change metres into centimetres to cut cloth.

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
steps: 1 m = 100 cm. Big unit to small unit: multiply.

quiz.q: 6 km = ? m
steps: 1 km = 1,000 m. Big unit to small unit: multiply.

quiz.q: Write 4 m 8 cm in centimetres.
quiz.mistake: Writes 4 and 8 side by side and forgets that 4 m is 400 cm

quiz.q: Write 2,750 m in km and m.
quiz.mistake: Splits the digits in the wrong place

quiz.q: Riya's saree is 550 cm long. How long is it in metres and centimetres?
Aisha ran 1 km 200 m. Joseph ran 1,020 m. Who ran farther?
quiz.explain: 1 km 200 m = 1,200 m. 1,200 m is more than 1,020 m.

quiz.q: Half a kilometre is how many metres?
Kabir cuts a 3 m ribbon into pieces of 25 cm for rakhis. How many pieces does he get?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3 × 25 without changing metres into centimetres

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I change kilometres into metres?'
teach.praise: Easy peasy! 1 km is 1,000 m, so I multiply by 1,000!
teach.nudge: How many metres are in 1 km? What do I do with that number?

revise.summary: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm and 1 km = 1,000 m. Multiply to change a big unit to a small one and divide to change a small unit to a big one.
focus: Change km to m and m to cm
Write mixed units in one unit
Split a length into km and m or m and cm
remember: Big to small: multiply. Small to big: divide.
traps: Don't write 4 m 8 cm as 48 cm; it is 408 cm.
Don't use 100 for km to m; use 1,000.
Change metres to cm before dividing into cm pieces.

topics.title: Double number lines and comparing heights

learn.hook: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat is about 182 m tall. How many of you, standing on each other's heads, would that be?
points: A double number line has metres on top and centimetres below, lined up: 1 m sits above 100 cm, 2 m above 200 cm.
Halfway between 0 m and 1 m is 50 cm. Halfway between 1 m and 2 m is 1 m 50 cm = 150 cm.
To find the difference between two heights, write them in the same unit and subtract.
To put heights in order, compare them in the same unit.
To find which length doubled gives another, halve it: half of 3 m is 1 m 50 cm.
learn.reallife: Tailors and carpenters use measuring tapes marked in both m and cm — a double number line!

quiz.q: On a double number line, which centimetre mark sits below 4 m?
quiz.explain: Each metre is 100 cm, so 4 m lines up with 4 × 100 = 400 cm.
steps: On a double number line, each metre lines up with 100 cm.

quiz.q: On a double number line, a mark is halfway between 2 m and 3 m. What is it in cm?
quiz.explain: Halfway between 200 cm and 300 cm is 250 cm.
steps: Halfway between them is 50 cm more than 200 cm.

quiz.q: The Statue of Unity is about 182 m tall. A temple tower is 66 m tall. How much taller is the statue?
steps: How much taller = bigger height − smaller height.

quiz.q: Statue P is 45 m tall, statue Q is 4,050 cm and statue R is 42 m 60 cm. Which is the tallest?
quiz.explain: In cm: P = 4,500 cm, Q = 4,050 cm, R = 4,260 cm. P is the tallest.
steps: 4,500 is the biggest, so P is the tallest.

quiz.q: A palm tree is 9 m 40 cm tall and a neem tree is 7 m 85 cm. What is the difference?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts metres and centimetres separately without borrowing

quiz.q: Which length, doubled, gives 3 m?
quiz.explain: 3 m = 300 cm. Half of 300 cm is 150 cm = 1 m 50 cm.
steps: To find what doubled gives 3 m, halve 3 m.

quiz.q: Rani's height is 1 m 20 cm. Her father is double her height. How tall is he?
Which length doubled gives 1 m 70 cm?
steps: To find what doubled gives 1 m 70 cm, halve it.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which is taller: a pole of 3 m 5 cm or one of 350 cm. How do I compare?
teach.praise: 3 m 5 cm is 305 cm, so the 350 cm pole is taller!
teach.nudge: What should I change both lengths into first?

revise.summary: A double number line lines up metres with centimetres. To compare or subtract heights, write them in the same unit; to find what doubles to a length, halve it.
focus: Read cm marks on a double number line
Find differences between heights
Order heights in mixed units
Halve or double lengths in m and cm
remember: 1 m sits above 100 cm, 2 m above 200 cm
Halfway between 2 m and 3 m is 250 cm
Half of 3 m is 1 m 50 cm
traps: Don't compare 45 m with 4,050 cm without changing units.
Don't halve or double only the metres.

topics.title: Steps, metres and distances from school

learn.hook: How many steps do you take to walk 100 m? Count them and you will have your own 'step ruler'!
points: Measure 100 m on the ground with a tape, then walk it and count your steps.
If you take 200 steps in 100 m, each step is about 50 cm, and 2 steps make about 1 m.
Use your steps to estimate other distances: 600 steps is about 300 m.
To order places by distance from school, write all distances in the same unit first.

example.q: Neel takes 160 steps for 100 m. The park is 480 steps away. About how far is it?
steps: So it is about 3 × 100 m = 300 m

learn.reallife: People used footsteps to measure land long ago. Even today, we say a shop is 'just 5 minutes' walk' away.

quiz.q: Mira takes 200 steps to walk 100 m. How many steps does she take for 300 m?
quiz.explain: 100 m takes 200 steps, so 300 m takes 3 × 200 = 600 steps.
quiz.mistake: Uses the same number of steps as metres

quiz.q: Arjun takes 200 steps in 100 m. About how long is one step?
With 2 steps for every metre, about how far is a shop that is 900 steps away?
Which place is nearest to school: library 750 m, bank 1 km 5 m, clinic 1,050 m?
quiz.explain: In metres: 750, 1,005 and 1,050. 750 is the smallest.
steps: Library 750 m, bank 1 km 5 m = 1,005 m, clinic 1,050 m.
750 m is the smallest, so the library is nearest.
quiz.mistake: Compares without changing to one unit

quiz.q: Which place is farthest: playground 1 km 200 m, lake 1,020 m, fort 1 km 80 m?
quiz.explain: In metres: 1,200, 1,020 and 1,080. The playground is farthest.
steps: Playground 1 km 200 m = 1,200 m, lake 1,020 m, fort 1 km 80 m = 1,080 m.
1,200 m is the biggest, so the playground is farthest.

quiz.q: Tina measures 200 m with a tape. Why does she count her steps over it?
options: To know about how many steps she takes for a known distance
To find the time of day
quiz.explain: Knowing steps for a known distance lets her estimate other distances.
steps: 200 m is a known distance measured with a tape.
Counting steps over it tells her how many steps make that distance.
So she knows about how many steps she takes for a known distance, to estimate others.
Answer: To know about how many steps she takes for a known distance
quiz.mistake: Does not see why a known length helps

quiz.q: Raj takes 140 steps for 100 m. His uncle takes 120 steps for 100 m. Who has the longer step?
quiz.explain: Fewer steps for the same distance means each step is longer.
steps: Fewer steps for the same distance means each step is longer: Uncle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more steps means longer steps

quiz.q: Put in order from nearest: A 2 km, B 1,800 m, C 2 km 50 m. Which is in the middle?
quiz.explain: 1,800 m < 2,000 m < 2,050 m. A (2 km) is in the middle.
steps: Write all in metres: A = 2,000 m, B = 1,800 m, C = 2,050 m.
Order from nearest: 1,800 < 2,000 < 2,050 → B, A, C.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know how far his nest is without a tape. How can my steps help?
teach.praise: First I count steps for 100 m, then use them to estimate any distance. Smart!
teach.nudge: How can I find out how long my step is?

revise.summary: Walk a measured 100 m and count your steps to know your step length. Then use steps to estimate other distances, and use one unit to order places by distance.
focus: Find step length from steps in a known distance
Estimate distances from steps
Order places by distance in mixed units
remember: 200 steps in 100 m means each step is about 50 cm
2 steps for every metre: metres = steps ÷ 2
Write all distances in the same unit before ordering
traps: More steps for the same distance means shorter steps, not longer.
Don't read 1 km 80 m as 1,800 m; it is 1,080 m.

learn.hook: Which is longer: 3 km 40 m or 3,400 m? They look alike, but they are not!
points: Before adding, subtracting or comparing, write both distances in the same unit.
1 km 50 m = 1,050 m, not 1,500 m. The 50 sits in the tens and ones places.
Add or subtract the numbers just like ordinary numbers.
Change the answer back to km and m if that is easier to read.

example.q: Harpreet walks 650 m to the bus stop and then rides 3 km 400 m by bus. How far does she travel?

learn.reallife: Train timetables list the distance between stations. Cyclists add up the kilometres of each ride.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put these distances from shortest to longest

games.title: True or false?
items: 1 km 5 m is the same as 1,005 m.
3 m = 300 cm, and 250 cm is less than 300 cm.
To add 2 km and 300 m, first write them in the same unit.
2 km = 2,000 m, so the total is 2,300 m.

quiz.q: A train goes from Rampur to Sitapur (64 km) and then from Sitapur to Gopalpur (96 km). How far is Rampur to Gopalpur on this route?
steps: The route goes Rampur → Sitapur → Gopalpur, so add the parts.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry when adding, or subtracts

quiz.q: Meena walked 1 km 250 m in the morning and 850 m in the evening. How many metres did she walk in all?
Arjun's school is 2 km from home. He has cycled 1 km 350 m. How much farther must he go?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing slip when subtracting from 2,000

quiz.q: Which is shorter: 3 km 40 m or 3,400 m?
quiz.explain: 3 km 40 m = 3,040 m, and 3,040 m is less than 3,400 m.

quiz.q: One lap of a running track is 400 m. How many laps make 2 km?
quiz.mistake: Divides 2 by 400 without changing km to m

quiz.q: Kabir's home is 750 m from the cycle shop. He goes to the shop and back home two times in a day. How far does he travel?
quiz.explain: Each round trip is 750 × 2 = 1,500 m. Two round trips: 3,000 m = 3 km.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one round trip, or only one way

quiz.q: Riya has 5 m of lace. She uses 1 m 75 cm to decorate a diya stand. How much lace is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the metres but forgets to borrow for the centimetres

quiz.q: A road sign says 'Jaipur 48 km'. Later another sign says 'Jaipur 19 km'. How far has the car gone between the signs?
steps: The car went from 48 km away to 19 km away.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two distances instead of finding the difference

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I add 1 km 250 m and 850 m?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Change both into metres first, then add: 2,100 m!
teach.nudge: Can I add km and m straight away? What should I do first?

revise.summary: Before adding, subtracting or comparing distances, write both in the same unit. Then work like ordinary numbers and change back to km and m if easier.
focus: Add distances in km and m
Find how much farther to go
Compare distances in mixed units
Find distance travelled between two road signs
traps: Don't forget the km part when adding the metres.
Don't add two road-sign distances; subtract them.
Don't read 3 km 40 m as 3,400 m.

topics.title: Kilometre race: markers on a route

learn.hook: A 3 km race needs a flag every 500 m, including the start and the finish. How many flags must you carry?
points: To place markers at equal gaps, divide the route length by the gap: 3,000 m ÷ 500 m = 6 gaps.
Markers are needed at the start and at the end of every gap, so markers = gaps + 1.
3 km with markers every 500 m: 6 gaps, so 7 markers.
Always change km to m before dividing by a gap in metres.

example.q: A 3 km route has a marker every 300 m, at start and finish too. How many markers?

learn.reallife: Water stations in a marathon and electric poles along a road are placed at equal gaps.

games.title: Gaps and markers
items: A 1 km route with markers every 500 m needs 3 markers.
Markers = gaps + 1 when both ends have a marker.
A 2 km route with a marker every 1 km has 2 markers.

quiz.q: A 3 km route has a marker every 500 m, including the start and finish. How many markers?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the marker at the start

quiz.q: How many gaps of 300 m are in 3 km?
steps: Change km to m: 3 km = 3,000 m.
quiz.mistake: Does not change km to m

quiz.q: A 3 km route has markers every 50 m, including both ends. How many markers?
A 2 km path has a bench every 250 m, including both ends. How many benches?
A race track has 11 markers at equal gaps of 100 m from start to finish. How long is it?
quiz.explain: 11 markers make 10 gaps. 10 × 100 m = 1,000 m = 1 km.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the markers instead of the gaps

quiz.q: Volunteers stand every 200 m on a 1 km route, but not at the start. How many volunteers?
quiz.explain: 1,000 ÷ 200 = 5 gaps. No one at the start, so 5 volunteers (at 200, 400, 600, 800, 1,000 m).
steps: Each gap ends with a volunteer at 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000 m.
No one at the start, so no extra 1: 5 volunteers.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 even though the start is left out

quiz.q: Flags are placed at 0 m, 400 m, 800 m … up to 2 km. How many flags?
Why is the number of markers one more than the number of gaps?
options: Because the route is in km
Because there is a marker at the start as well as at the end of each gap
quiz.explain: Each gap ends at a marker, and one more marker stands at the very start.
steps: Each gap ends at a marker.
There is also one marker at the very start, before the first gap.
So markers = gaps + 1, because there is a marker at the start as well as at the end of each gap.
Answer: Because there is a marker at the start as well as at the end of each gap

teach.ask: Gappu must put a tree every 100 m along a 1 km road, at both ends too. How many trees do I need?
teach.praise: 1,000 ÷ 100 = 10 gaps, plus 1 for the start: 11 trees!
teach.nudge: How many gaps are there, and is a tree at the start too?

revise.summary: To place markers at equal gaps, divide the route length by the gap. Markers are at the start and at the end of every gap, so markers = gaps + 1.
focus: Find the number of gaps on a route
Find the number of markers including both ends
Adjust when the start has no marker
remember: Markers = gaps + 1 (when both ends have one)
3 km with markers every 500 m: 6 gaps, 7 markers
traps: Change km to m before dividing by a gap in m.
Don't add 1 when there is no marker at the start.

learn.hook: One of India's longest train journeys covers over 4,000 km! A table of distances helps us find how far it is between any two stations.
points: Some timetables show distance from the first station: this is a cumulative (running total) distance.
Distance between two stations = bigger running total − smaller running total.
Read the station's row carefully before subtracting.
Compare the distances between pairs of stations to find the longest or shortest part.

example.q: Table: Amgaon 0 km, Bhimpur 312 km, Chandanpur 1,045 km. How far is Bhimpur to Chandanpur?

learn.reallife: Railway timetables print 'distance from start' so travellers can work out how far they go.

quiz.q: Table (distance from Amgaon): Bhimpur 312 km, Chandanpur 1,045 km. How far is Bhimpur from Chandanpur?
steps: Both distances are from Amgaon (running totals).

quiz.q: Chandanpur is 1,045 km and Devgarh is 2,380 km from Amgaon. How far apart are they?
Devgarh is 2,380 km and Ekpur 4,189 km from Amgaon. How far from Devgarh to Ekpur?
In the table, what does 'Bhimpur 312 km' mean?
options: Bhimpur is 312 km from the next station
Bhimpur is 312 km from the last station
Bhimpur is 312 km from the first station, Amgaon
quiz.explain: The table shows distance from the starting station.
steps: The table gives distance from the first station (a running total).
So Bhimpur is 312 km from the first station, Amgaon.
Answer: Bhimpur is 312 km from the first station, Amgaon
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is the distance from the station before

quiz.q: Table: Bhimpur 312 km, Chandanpur 1,045 km, Devgarh 2,380 km from Amgaon. Which station is 1,045 km from Amgaon?
quiz.explain: Read along the table: the row with 1,045 km is Chandanpur.
steps: Look down the distance column for 1,045 km.
Bhimpur is 312, Chandanpur is 1,045, Devgarh is 2,380.
So Chandanpur is 1,045 km from Amgaon.

quiz.q: Which part is longest: Amgaon–Bhimpur (312 km), Bhimpur–Chandanpur (733 km) or Chandanpur–Devgarh (1,335 km)?
quiz.explain: 1,335 km is the biggest of the three.
steps: Compare the three parts: 312 km, 733 km, 1,335 km.
So Chandanpur–Devgarh is the longest part.
quiz.mistake: Picks the part with the biggest station number

quiz.q: Riya travels from Bhimpur (312 km) to Devgarh (2,380 km). How far does she go?
quiz.mistake: Uses only one part of the trip

quiz.q: Is Bhimpur–Chandanpur (733 km) longer or shorter than Devgarh–Ekpur (1,809 km)? By how much?
steps: 733 km is less than 1,809 km, so Bhimpur–Chandanpur is shorter.

teach.ask: Gappu's table says Ranipur 450 km and Sonpur 1,200 km from the start. How far is Ranipur to Sonpur?
teach.praise: 1,200 − 450 = 750 km. The table shows distance from the start!
teach.nudge: What do the numbers in the table measure from?

revise.summary: A train table often shows the distance of each station from the first station, a running total. Distance between two stations = bigger total − smaller total.
focus: Read a running-total distance table
Find the distance between two stations
Compare parts of a route
remember: Distance between stations = bigger running total − smaller running total
traps: Don't add the two distances from the table.
The table distance is from the first station, not the station before.

learn.hook: A sprouting moong seed grows only a few millimetres a day. How do we measure something that tiny?
points: 1 centimetre = 10 millimetres (mm). The tiny lines between cm marks on a ruler are millimetres.
To measure, start at 0. A line ending 3 small marks after 5 cm is 5 cm 3 mm = 53 mm.
Seeds grow by small amounts, so we record their growth in mm.
To draw a line of 4 cm 5 mm, start at 0 and stop at the 5th small mark after 4 cm.
Growth = new length − old length.

example.q: A sprout was 4 mm on Monday and 1 cm 3 mm on Thursday. How much did it grow?

learn.reallife: Doctors, jewellers and engineers measure tiny lengths in millimetres. Rain is measured in mm too!

items.text: A line from 0 to the 7th small mark after 3 cm is ___ mm
A 2 cm 5 mm line is ___ mm

quiz.q: How many millimetres are there in 7 cm?
A pencil lead line ends 4 small marks after the 6 cm mark (starting at 0). How long is it?
quiz.explain: 6 cm and 4 small mm marks: 6 cm 4 mm.
steps: The line starts at 0 and passes the 6 cm mark.
So it is 6 cm 4 mm long.

quiz.q: A seed sprout was 3 mm on Day 1 and 12 mm on Day 4. How much did it grow?
Write 4 cm 5 mm in millimetres.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits with a 0 between them

quiz.q: An eraser starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at 5 cm 6 mm. How long is it?
quiz.mistake: Forgets it did not start at 0

quiz.q: To draw a line 38 mm long, where should Ravi stop his pencil?
options: At the 3rd small mark after 8 cm
At the 8th small mark after 3 cm
steps: Change 38 mm into cm and mm: 38 ÷ 10 = 3 cm with 8 mm left.
So stop at the 8th small mark after 3 cm.
Answer: At the 8th small mark after 3 cm

quiz.q: Which is the best unit to measure the thickness of a coin?
quiz.explain: A coin is only about 1–2 mm thick, so mm is best.
steps: A coin is only about 1–2 mm thick.
km, m and even cm are too big for that.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit that is too big

quiz.q: A bean sprout grows 2 mm every day. How long will it be after 6 days, if it starts at 5 mm?

teach.ask: Gappu's feather measures 3 cm and 7 tiny marks. How long is it in mm?
teach.praise: 3 cm is 30 mm, plus 7 mm makes 37 mm!
teach.nudge: How many millimetres make one centimetre?

revise.summary: 1 cm = 10 mm; the tiny lines between cm marks on a ruler are millimetres. Small growth, like a sprout's, is recorded in mm, and growth = new length − old length.
focus: Change cm to mm
Read and draw lengths in cm and mm
Find growth in mm
traps: Don't use 100 mm in a cm.
Don't forget the starting length when something grows each day.

learn.hook: Simran has two ribbons: 2 m 75 cm and 1 m 50 cm. Is that enough to tie a 4 m border?
points: mm to cm and mm: divide by 10. 47 mm = 4 cm 7 mm. cm and mm to mm: 8 cm 2 mm = 82 mm.
To add lengths in m and cm, add cm to cm and m to m. If cm make 100 or more, change 100 cm into 1 m.
2 m 75 cm + 1 m 50 cm = 3 m 125 cm = 4 m 25 cm.
To find the bigger length and the difference, change both into the same unit first.

example.q: Which is longer, 2 km 80 m or 2,600 m? By how much?

learn.reallife: Tailors add up lengths of cloth, and drivers compare distances in km and m on road signs.

quiz.q: Write 47 mm in cm and mm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mm and cm are the same size

quiz.q: Write 8 cm 2 mm in mm.
Simran joins ribbons of 2 m 75 cm and 1 m 50 cm. How long is the ribbon now?
quiz.mistake: Does not change 100 cm into 1 m

quiz.q: Kabir has 1 m 65 cm of rope and buys 85 cm more. How much rope does he have?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry from cm to m

quiz.q: Which is longer: 2 km 80 m or 2,600 m?
quiz.explain: 2 km 80 m = 2,080 m, which is less than 2,600 m.
steps: Write both in metres: 2 km 80 m = 2,000 + 80 = 2,080 m.

quiz.q: How much longer is 2,600 m than 2 km 80 m?
Which is bigger: 5 m 6 cm or 560 cm? What is the difference?
A strip of 9 cm 6 mm and one of 3 cm 8 mm are joined. How long is the joined strip in mm?
steps: Change to mm: 9 cm 6 mm = 96 mm, 3 cm 8 mm = 38 mm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change cm to mm or to carry

teach.ask: Gappu has a twig of 1 m 70 cm and another of 60 cm. How long are they together?
teach.nudge: What do I do when the centimetres add up to more than 100?

revise.summary: Divide mm by 10 to get cm and mm. Add lengths unit by unit and change every 100 cm into 1 m; change both lengths to one unit before finding the difference.
focus: Change between mm and cm-and-mm
Add lengths in m and cm with carrying
Find which length is longer and by how much
remember: 47 mm = 4 cm 7 mm; 8 cm 2 mm = 82 mm
2 m 75 cm + 1 m 50 cm = 4 m 25 cm
traps: Don't leave 125 cm; change it to 1 m 25 cm.

learn.hook: Amma needs 4 curtains, each 2 m 25 cm long. How much cloth should she buy, and what will it cost?
points: To multiply a length in m and cm, change it to cm, multiply, then change back: 3 m 25 cm × 4 = 325 × 4 = 1,300 cm = 13 m.
Cost of 1 metre = total cost ÷ number of metres. If 5 m cost ₹450, 1 m costs ₹90.
A double number line helps: 5 m ↔ ₹450, so 1 m ↔ ₹90 and 3 m ↔ ₹270.
Total cost = total length × cost of 1 m.
To share a length equally, change to the smaller unit and divide: 12 km 600 m ÷ 3 = 12,600 m ÷ 3 = 4,200 m.

example.q: 4 curtains each need 2 m 25 cm of cloth at ₹80 a metre. Find the length and the cost.

learn.reallife: Cloth shops sell by the metre, and road builders divide long roads into equal parts for teams.

learn.hook: How tall is your school building? You can estimate it without climbing up — just use something you know!
points: Estimate a big height using a known one: if one floor is about 3 m, a 5-floor building is about 15 m.
Depths can be estimated the same way: a well as deep as 4 men of about 1 m 50 cm is about 6 m deep.
Some people use inches and feet. 1 inch is about 2 cm 5 mm.
1 foot = 12 inches, which is about 30 cm.
Height in feet and inches: 4 feet 6 inches = 4 × 12 + 6 = 54 inches.

example.q: Megha is 4 feet 5 inches tall. How many inches is that?

learn.reallife: TV screens are sold in inches and many people tell their height in feet and inches.

quiz.q: A building has 6 floors. Each floor is about 3 m high. About how tall is it?
steps: Height ≈ number of floors × height of one floor.

steps: One floor is about 3 m high.
